synthesis: The prime-orbit dictionary fixes primitive periods as log p and therefore fixes log 2 as the shortest period. At the distinct long-orbit scale needed to resolve mean-spaced levels, orbit proliferation cancels squared-amplitude decay in the Hannay-Ozorio sum rule and removes system detail; at the short-orbit scale, failure of that sum rule restores the log 2 datum and predicts the growing separation at which Riemann-zero statistics depart from GUE. The same period assignment thus determines both the local universal regime and its nonuniform boundary.
source_support: Unit u04 matches primes and prime powers to primitive orbits and repetitions, periods to log p, exact amplitude decay to unit instability, and the prefactor to broken time reversal. Unit u05 identifies the Heisenberg-time orbit range required for individual-level resolution. Unit u06 derives the long-orbit universal sum rule from proliferation balanced by intensity decay and connects it to invariant measure. Unit u07 states that short orbits violate that long-orbit rule and uses T0=log 2 to predict breakdown beyond about log(t/2pi)/log 2 mean spacings.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes the trace-formula representation with two different resolution limits: the long-orbit sum rule erases orbit identity at mean spacing, while inverse period-to-energy scaling converts the shortest prime orbit into a quantitative boundary of that erasure.
limits: The Euler-product comparison in the critical strip is formal and the generic trace formula is semiclassical; exact amplitudes, phases, determinants, and breakdown constants are formula-sensitive. Agreement constrains a hypothetical dynamics but neither constructs it nor proves RH, and universality is asserted only for fixed local separations in the asymptotic limit.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct units supply a concrete chain from coefficient-level prime-orbit matching through Heisenberg-time resolution and ergodic cancellation to a shortest-orbit breakdown scale; neither the universality mechanism nor its boundary is available from any one parent alone.

synthesis: The diagonal orbit sum and the Hannay-Ozorio rule produce K(tau)=|tau| only below the Heisenberg threshold; discreteness then forces coherent off-diagonal cancellation rather than random-phase disappearance. For Riemann zeros, Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair correlations supply that missing long-time contribution, while retaining short prime orbits and then the unsmoothed singular series separates two finite-height effects: low zeta zeros reappear as resonances in high-zero correlations, and fine arithmetic phases produce the small oscillatory correction to number variance.
source_support: Unit u09 derives the diagonal form factor and shows that K tending to one requires destructive off-diagonal interference for large tau. Unit u10 derives the required off-diagonal limit from the averaged Hardy-Littlewood defect and retains explicit short-orbit terms. Unit u11 rewrites the short-prime correction through log zeta, making low zeros resonances in high-zero correlations. Unit u12 replaces the smoothed input by the full singular series to recover small oscillations and states why generic dynamics lacks the required action-correlation input. Unit u13 constructs a truncated implicit spectrum and gives only a heuristic reverse route to Hardy-Littlewood-type correlations.
nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes the form factor by orbit pairing, uses discreteness to infer the sign and size of missing coherence, then tracks what successive arithmetic compressions lose: smoothing retains the universal off-diagonal limit, explicit short terms retain resonance data, and unsmoothing restores fine phase oscillations.
limits: The off-diagonal Riemann derivation depends on the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture and the full GUE statement is Montgomery-conjectural in this account. Exact scalings, Euler products, and Fourier conventions are formula-sensitive. The reverse construction is semiclassical and heuristic, and without an analogue of prime-pair correlations it cannot recover system-specific corrections for generic chaotic systems.
quality_reason: Accepted because the five units jointly establish a staged mechanism from diagonal failure to arithmetic coherence and then to two distinct nonuniversal corrections, while explicitly preserving the conjectural and solver-specific limits; this is more than a shared theme or restatement of one unit.

synthesis: For zeta, the functional equation pairs the divergent long tail with conjugates of the early Dirichlet terms at the stationary cutoff, yielding a finite real main sum. For a Hermitian quantum problem, reality of the spectral determinant plays the analogous role: after reorganizing primitive orbits into composite pseudo-orbits, analytic continuation pairs contributions across half the Heisenberg time to give a finite real determinant formula. Abrupt cutoffs in both representations create discontinuities, motivating local Riemann-Siegel corrections on the zeta side and an Erfc-smoothed transition that also transfers to the quantum determinant.
source_support: Unit u15 derives the stationary Riemann-Siegel cutoff and conjugate tail resummation from the functional equation. Units u16 and u17 show how cutoff-local coefficients repair jumps and how factorial growth fixes least-term accuracy. Unit u18 expands the Hermitian spectral determinant over pseudo-orbits, locates the cutoff at TH/2, and pairs long and short contributions by analytic continuation. Unit u19 supplies Erfc smoothing, explicit corrections, its quantum adaptation, and a separate heuristic reading of exp(-pi t) as an imaginary-period orbit.
nonparaphrase_operation: Transfers a long-short duality only after changing representation from additive primitive-orbit data to a multiplicative determinant indexed by composite pseudo-orbits, then identifies cutoff discontinuity as the common defect and smoothing as the shared repair rather than merely noting parallel formulas.
limits: The zeta correction hierarchy is asymptotic, with formula-sensitive coefficients and least-term conventions. The quantum lookalike is semiclassical, has exponentially many pseudo-orbits in dimension greater than one, and lacks the direct Riemann-Siegel correction machinery; its smoothed version is supported by a reported numerical test, not an exact general identity. The imaginary-period interpretation is explicitly heuristic and constructs no Riemann dynamics.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct units support both the representation change that makes conjugate pairing transferable and the shared cutoff-repair mechanism, while also showing that the zeta and quantum cases differ sharply in exactness, computational cost, and available corrections.

Testing that package against the coupled Riemann-dynamics constraints localizes the failure at spectral closure: dilation sums can contain zeta without enforcing its zeros, character twists only suggest unconstructed boundary extensions, and position-momentum reinjection gives the near-zero identity with the wrong sign while leaving boundedness, prime primitive periods, and Maslov phases unresolved.

nonparaphrase_operation: Performs a coupled constraint audit: it traces several apparent matches to their common dilation representation, then tests whether the proposed symmetry and boundary routes convert analytic occurrence into a self-adjoint discrete spectrum, exposing independent structural and sign obstructions.
limits: XP remains a tentative formal Hamiltonian. Its mean-count match uses an ad hoc cutoff; the even continuation and Fourier factors are convention-sensitive; no self-adjoint compactification or discrete spectrum is supplied. quality_reason: Accepted because six units jointly support a concrete gain-loss diagnosis: the same dilation structure explains multiple analytic and dynamical clues, but separate boundary experiments demonstrate why those matches do not enforce Riemann zeros. The synthesis preserves the decisive distinction between syntactic appearance of zeta and spectral realization.
